finding:
The printed fixed-stage claim is for every second-countable Hausdorff locally compact abelian G with a continuous proper surjective module ν=|·|_G:G→ℝ_{>0}, every nonempty real interval I (including singletons; no requirement that 0∈I), and every compact subgroup k with compactly generated annihilator in the full Pontryagin dual. Remark D.2.1.2 states existence of a continuous homomorphic section. The p. 804 setup distinguishes compact generation of the full annihilator from finite generation of the annihilator in the discrete dual of the compact kernel G¹. Every compact k lies in G¹ because the positive reals have no nontrivial compact subgroup. The full annihilator contains the radial dual ℝ, so the “finitely generated” wording of the inductive-limit paragraph on p. 805 cannot literally be used for the full dual; p. 11 and the stage definition on p. 805 say compactly generated. In split coordinates the admissible compact quotient G¹/k is a torus times a finite abelian group, not necessarily a point or finite. For example, take G=ℝ_{>0}×𝕋 with projection module and k trivial; the full dual ℝ×ℤ is compactly generated.

At p. 11 φ is smooth; Definition D.3.3.1 uses continuous φ with every weighted function in S(G). For the fixed k-invariant stage the actual profiles can be read on G/k, with every ν^aφ Schwartz–Bruhat there, and with the induced topology from the entire product of copies of S(k,G)=S(G/k) under φ↦(ν^aφ)_{a∈I}. Here ν descends and is smooth in the elementary Lie quotient coordinates, so one weighted Schwartz profile already supplies smoothness after multiplication by its smooth inverse weight. This uses the quotient Schwartz–Bruhat seminorm topology, not pointwise convergence or just continuity of the profiles: D.1.3.1 controls polynomial weights in noncompact coordinates and all derivatives, including the torus directions, and D.1.5.3 transports that topology to the quotient stage. The p. 11 topology is defined by all weights, not by an arbitrary chosen topology on a function space; Example D.3.3.5 gives the endpoint and countable closed-product route to the separate nuclear Fréchet assertion. Scope is the stage, not the later strict LF, full-space completeness, Montel or bounded-set comparisons.

The sentence after (1.1.2.1) prints the completed projective tensor S_I(ℝ_{>0}) ⊗̂_π S(G¹/k) without naming a split. The appendix makes the map depend on a chosen continuous homomorphic section τ with ν∘τ=id. In G/k, the inverse coordinates are ([g]↦(ν(g),[τ(ν(g))⁻¹g])), so the natural elementary-tensor formula is f(ν(g))h([τ(ν(g))⁻¹g]). This is the split-coordinate reading of “This is also,” not a section-free equality of carriers. For instance in ℝ_{>0}×𝕋 replacing τ(t)=(t,1) by (t,e^{ic log t}) changes the compact argument of a nonconstant h. The stage itself and its weighted topology do not use τ. The bars over the tensor in (D.3.3.3)–(D.3.3.5) on the left and on the source of the stage arrow (D.3.3.7) denote the COMPLETED inductive tensor, not ⊗_ι on the incomplete algebraic tensor. (D.3.3.5) compares it with the completed projective tensor on the fixed factors (up to the order of factors); Corollary C.2.3.12 compares the uncompleted topologies first, then their completions. The full-space bounded-set map (D.3.3.6) is a different claim, not the fixed-stage arrow. The p. 810 proof of D.3.3.7(1) invokes (D.3.3.7) and the comparison of completions; footnote 21 flags no contact with the stages, possible circularity, and that the overbar-tensor version of (D.3.3.7) has not been proved there. That is a proof gap, not a refutation, and not the reason this statement lane is blocked.

Representation audit at accepted base 7baa8bac78e3e259acf66e83a858a8d87886f7d2 (session 01a20638-495e-7650-b8d6-f5417d7c83aa; Lean v4.36.0, Mathlib fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842): `IsProperMap` and a continuous homomorphism into `Multiplicative ℝ` can express the logarithmic module, and the compact-open `PontryaginDual`, `Subgroup.closure`, and quotient-group APIs can express literal admissibility and the quotient carriers. In a scratch probe, `IsCompact (k : Set G) ∧ ∃ K : Set (PontryaginDual G), IsCompact K ∧ (Subgroup.closure K : Set (PontryaginDual G)) = {χ | ∀ x : k, χ x.1 = 1}` elaborated, as did `G ⧸ k` and `ν.toMonoidHom.ker ⧸ k.subgroupOf ν.toMonoidHom.ker`. This is algebraic generation by a compact subset, not topological closure of a generated subgroup. The quotient-to-elementary-coordinates bridge was not supplied by these carrier checks. `Masullo.continuousMulEquivOfSection` (Proofs/Lemmas/ContinuousNormSplit.lean) is the group-level split given a central section and its right-inverse law; it neither produces the section nor supplies the function-space topology or map. `Masullo.logWeightedStage` and its complete, metrizable, locally convex results in Proofs/Theorems/RadialWeightedSchwartz{Stage,Frechet}.lean are the identity-module logarithmic line with trivial compact factor; see the unsuffixed proof receipt for this key/revision and .godel/formalize/radial-weighted-frechet.md. The specialized additive rational adele stages / finest stagewise seminorm topology in Proofs/Props/RationalAdeleSchwartzLF.lean do not model these quotients of general modulated G.

The missing first objects are the source-topologized S(G¹/k) and S(G/k) on the admissible quotients and hence the actual weighted fixed stage of (1.1.2.1). Mathlib's `SchwartzMap` is for normed real vector domains and their iterated Fréchet derivatives. Its application even to the log-coordinate example `SchwartzMap (ℝ × Circle) ℂ` fails at `NormedAddCommGroup (ℝ × Circle)`; lifting to a periodic function on ℝ² and imposing the full ordinary ℝ² Schwartz decay would force it to vanish. `ContMDiffMap` supplies manifold smoothness but not the mixed decay/seminorm topology. The second missing object is the separated completion of the complex algebraic tensor with the general locally convex projective topology of the actual factors. `TensorProduct` is algebraic; `PiTensorProduct.projectiveSeminorm` exists but uses one seminormed-space structure on each input, not the family of continuous factor seminorms. Its application to two copies of the genuine radial stage for I=[1,3] already fails to find `SeminormedAddCommGroup` on that stage. `UniformSpace.Completion` takes a supplied uniformity and cannot supply the projective one. Finally, completeness, metrizability, Hausdorffness and local convexity are available notions, but I did not find a definition of nuclearity for this topology as in C.2.4.1 or a usable equivalent in the project or pinned Mathlib. The deprecated `PiTensorProduct.injectiveSeminorm` is explicitly not the mathematical ε construction and is extensionally equal to the projective seminorm in its own API; using it as the comparison would make nuclearity vacuous. These findings come from inspecting the actual project definitions and Mathlib Schwartz, manifold maps, Pontryagin dual, projective/injective seminorm and completion interfaces, with scoped source searches for Schwartz–Bruhat, nuclearity and topological tensor definitions, not a claim that Lean cannot express them.
